precepts.text: The sanctuary is dedicated again on the very day the heathen had profaned it, the dedication Daniel's cleansing points to.
precepts.point: The cleansing of the sanctuary goes into Hanukkah, the feast of dedication. That history is recorded in First Maccabees.

note.label: Daniel 8: The Ram and the Goat

precepts.why:
The saint asked “How long shall be the vision concerning the daily sacrifice, and the transgression of desolation, to give both the sanctuary and the host to be trodden under foot?” and the answer was “Unto two thousand and three hundred days; then shall the sanctuary be cleansed.” The cleansing of the sanctuary goes into Hanukkah, the feast of dedication, and that history is recorded in First Maccabees.

“Now on the five and twentieth day of the ninth month, which is called the month Casleu, in the hundred forty and eighth year, they rose up betimes in the morning, And offered sacrifice according to the law upon the new altar of burnt offerings, which they had made.” The daily sacrifice was offered again, according to the law, upon a new altar.

“Look, at what time and what day the heathen had profaned it, even in that was it dedicated with songs, and citherns, and harps, and cymbals.” The sanctuary was dedicated again on the very day the heathen had profaned it. That dedication, on the twenty-fifth day of the month Casleu, is what Daniel's cleansing of the sanctuary points to.

precepts.text: The standard for the body is blameless conversation and pleasure in the law of the Most High.
precepts.point: Fear came on every soul, and all that believed were together and had all things common. Having all things common means the same speech and the same mind, perfectly joined together, with blameless conversation and pleasure in the law, so that when the mind is fixed on the law, materialistic things stop mattering.

note.label: Acts 2: Pentecost and the Scattered House of Israel

precepts.why:
When the sanctuary was cleansed, Judas “chose priests of blameless conversation, such as had pleasure in the law”. That is the standard for the body: blameless conversation and pleasure in the law of the Most High.

Having all things common means the same speech and the same mind, perfectly joined together. When the mind is fixed on the law, materialistic things stop mattering, which is how all that believed could be together, sell their possessions and goods, and part them to every man as he had need.

precepts.text: Judas said the enemies, the Greeks, were discomfited, so they went up to dedicate the sanctuary.
precepts.point: The feast of dedication Christ kept in John 10 commemorates the Maccabees driving out the Greeks and rededicating the temple the Greeks had profaned. Christ would not turn around a few months later and accept those same Greeks.

note.label: Acts 6: The Grecians Were Greek-Speaking Israelites

precepts.why:
“Then said Judas and his brethren, Behold, our enemies are discomfited: let us go up to cleanse and dedicate the sanctuary.”

The enemies who were discomfited were the Greeks. That is the dedication of the sanctuary the feast of dedication in John 10 remembers, and it is why Christ, who kept that feast, was not accepting Greeks as his own a few months later. The Grecians of Acts 6 are Israelites, not the enemies Judas drove out.

precepts.text: The temple was rededicated on the very day the heathen had profaned it.
precepts.point: Read logically, using comparison and context. Christianity teaches people to read the bible with a slave mind, taking a verse at face value the way the slave master intended, instead of going back to the beginning as you would with any book or film.

note.label: Acts 6: The Grecians Were Greek-Speaking Israelites

precepts.why:
“Look, at what time and what day the heathen had profaned it, even in that was it dedicated with songs, and citherns, and harps, and cymbals.”

The temple was rededicated on the very day the heathen had profaned it, and the heathen were the Greeks. That is the feast of dedication Christ kept in John 10, and it shows who the Greeks were to Israel: the profaners of the sanctuary, not brethren in the church.
